column3: Close to the Hebrew.
“Ancestor” is rendered “father.”
“In eight years” is rendered “in the eighth year,” and “cleanse” as “purge.” “Asherah poles” is rendered “Asherim.”
“People pulled down before him” is rendered “they tore down … in his presence”; NASB supplies “of those.”
“Cleansed” is rendered “purged.”
The final phrase is obscure in Hebrew; NASB follows the reading “in their surrounding ruins,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“Crushed to pulverize” is rendered “beat … into powder.”
“To cleanse the land” is rendered “when he had purged the land.”
NASB follows the reading read aloud, “the inhabitants of Jerusalem,” for the written “they returned to Jerusalem.” “Keepers of the threshold” is rendered “doorkeepers.”
“Who were appointed in the house” is rendered “who had the oversight of the house,” and “mend” as “restore.”
“Craftsmen” is rendered “carpenters,” and “stones of hewing” as “quarried stone.” “Ruined” is rendered “had let go to ruin.”
“Instruments of song” is rendered “musical instruments”; NASB reorders the verse.
“For labor and labor” is rendered “from job to job.”
“By the hand of Moses” is rendered “given by Moses.”
“Answered” is rendered “responded.”
“Brought back again a word” is rendered “reported further word,” and “given in the hand of” as “entrusted to.”
“Poured out” is rendered “emptied out,” and “those who were appointed” as “the supervisors.”
“Read aloud in it” is rendered “read from it.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Consult” is rendered “inquire of,” and “the remnant” as “those who are left.” “Took care … to observe” is rendered “have not observed.”
The Hebrew lacks a verb after “the king”; NASB supplies “had told.” “Keeper of the garments” is rendered “keeper of the wardrobe,” and “like this” as “regarding this.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Harm” is rendered “evil.”
“Made smoke” is rendered “burned incense”; NASB supplies “therefore.”
NASB supplies “regarding.”
“Soft” is rendered “tender”; “the utterance of Yahweh” is rendered “declares the LORD.” NASB supplies “you” and “truly.”
“Graves” is rendered “grave,” and “distress” as “evil.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“From great and unto small” is rendered “from the greatest to the least,” and “in their ears” as “in their hearing.”
